conventions.source: Nielsen and Chuang, Quantum Computation and Quantum Information
conventions.wire_order: wire 1 is the top wire of the drawing and the most significant bit: amplitude k belongs to the basis label |w1 w2 ... wn> that is k in binary (opposite of Qiskit)
conventions.wire_numbers: 1-based in every user-facing structure; 0-based only inside the engine
conventions.rotations: R_a(theta) = exp(-i theta sigma_a / 2) for a in x, y, z
conventions.two_qubit_rotations: R_aa(theta) = exp(-i theta sigma_a ⊗ sigma_a / 2) for a in x, y, z
conventions.phase: P(theta) = diag(1, e^{i theta}); S = P(pi/2); T = P(pi/4)
conventions.controls: a closed control acts on |1>, an open control on |0>; any gate takes any number of controls, and controls are never part of the gate's own matrix
conventions.equality: equal up to global phase: max |a - e^{i phi} b| < 1e-9, with phi taken from the largest entry of b; exact equality is reported too
conventions.input_state: |0...0> unless the request gives a basis label or a list of amplitudes
conventions.step_order: operations apply left to right, in the order of Circuit.ops
conventions.measurement: version 1: computational-basis measurement at the end of a wire only; no operation may touch a wire after its measurement, and classically controlled operations are refused

conventions.rotations: R_a(theta) = exp(-i theta sigma_a / 2) for a in x, y, z
conventions.two_qubit_rotations: R_aa(theta) = exp(-i theta sigma_a ⊗ sigma_a / 2) for a in x, y, z
conventions.phase: P(theta) = diag(1, e^{i theta}); S = P(pi/2); T = P(pi/4)
conventions.controls: a closed control acts on |1>, an open control on |0>; any gate takes any number of controls, and controls are never part of the gate's own matrix
conventions.equality: equal up to global phase: max |a - e^{i phi} b| < 1e-9, with phi taken from the largest entry of b; exact equality is reported too
conventions.input_state: |0...0> unless the request gives a basis label or a list of amplitudes
conventions.step_order: operations apply left to right, in the order of Circuit.ops
conventions.measurement: version 1: computational-basis measurement at the end of a wire only; no operation may touch a wire after its measurement, and classically controlled operations are refused
